tagline: Route 28 across the Central Catskills, Andes to the Ashokan.
intro: Route 28 starts out from Andes, a town named in jest by a man who saw it took in one of the hilliest parts of the county, and runs through Margaretville in the valley of the East Branch of the Delaware. From there it goes by Fleischmanns and Pine Hill to Phoenicia, where Stony Clove Creek meets the Esopus, and on to the Ashokan Reservoir in the town of Olive.

The Ulster and Delaware Railroad reached these villages in the 1870s, and the summer people came up with it. The byway's 52 miles, with short spurs on Routes 42 and 214, celebrate the Catskill Park and the reservoirs of the New York City watershed.

moments.title: Fleischmanns
moments.text: In 1883 the yeast and whiskey maker Charles Fleischmann bought land by the depot, and his family's summer colony later had major league ballplayers, Honus Wagner among them, getting in shape here.

moments.title: Phoenicia
moments.text: Under Mount Tremper, Romer and Sheridan mountains, a railway museum opened in the old station in 1960, and in 1986 a two-ton iron eagle from Grand Central Depot settled here.

moments.title: Shokan
moments.text: The hamlet moved to where it stands when the Ashokan Reservoir flooded its old site, one of a dozen valley communities and some 2,000 people the water displaced.
